text.p: Italian serie A games due to be played on Saturday and Sunday, kick-off times GMT.

The Lazio renaissance under new coach Dino Zoff has proved shortlived with the side well beaten 2-0 by Parma on Sunday. Without striker Pierluigi Casiraghi, Australian Paul Okon and midfielder Giorgio Venturin, all injured, Lazio will hope Fiorentina are distracted by their Cup Winners' Cup tie with Portuguese side Benfica next week. Russian Andrei Kanchelskis, Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Anselmo Robbiati, scorer of Fiorentina's equaliser in their 1-1 draw with Juventus last Sunday, lead the Fiorentina attack.

Inter have a lot going against them. Not only are their thoughts fixed on Tuesday's UEFA Cup tie with Belgian side Anderlecht, but they received a double body-blow in midweek with their Italian Cup semifinal elimination by Napoli coming just hours after the announcement their English coach Roy Hodgson will be leaving at the end of the season to join Blackburn Rovers in England. Piacenza, led by Pasquale Luiso in attack, will hope to benefit from Inter's distractions. English midfielder Paul Ince and striker Marco Branca are doubtful starters for Inter whose attack will be led by Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff, Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Maurizio Ganz.

Atalanta's ten game, three month long unbeaten run finally ended with their 2-0 away loss to Inter on Sunday on a day when Perugia pulled off their biggest win of the season, defeating AC Milan 1-0. Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri lead the Perugia attack, while the league's leading goalscorer, Filippo Inzaghi on the 15 mark, leads the Atalanta front line.
AC MILAN (11) V AS ROMA (6), SUNDAY, 14.00

Croat Zvonimir Boban, Dutchman Edgar Davids, Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic, Swede Jesper Blomqvst, Frenchman Christophe Dugarry and Paolo Maldini are all ruled out of the Milan side either through suspension or injury. Which means that coach Arrigo Sacchi may turn to Roberto Baggio to resolve his ongoing crisis. Roma, held to an unimpressive 2-2 draw by bottom side Reggiana last week, have doubts about Argentine striker Abel Balbo but can take comfort from their comprehensive 3-0 win in Rome last October.

Tough assignment for relegation battling Cagliari against much improved Parma. Uruguyan Dario Silva and Sandro Tovalieri lead the Cagliari attack against Parma's first choice strike force of Enrico Chiesa and Argentine Hernan Crespo.

This could prove the most entertaining game of the day between two in-form, attacking sides. Sampdoria hit the woodwork three times in an unlucky 1-1 draw with Napoli last week while Bologna were last minute losers of their midweek Italian Cup semi-final tie with Vicenza. Sampdoria will be without Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic, replaced by Frenchman Oumar Dieng, but are led by terrible twins Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella in attack. Bologna field their strongest attack, led by Swede Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolyvanov.

If Napoli have recovered from celebrating their midweek Italian Cup semi-final win against Inter, they could prove an awkward customer for Udinese. German Oliver Bierhoff and Brazilian Amoroso lead the Udinese attack while Brazilian Beto again replaces injured compatriot Andre Cruz in the Napoli midfield behind strikers Nicola Caccia and Alfredo Aglietti.

Perhaps only honour is at stake in this battle between the bottom two sides in the league, both seemingly relegation bound. Belgian Georges Grun steps in for the suspended Filippo Galli in the Reggiana defence with the attack again being led by Russian Igor Simutenkov. Verona rely on their normal strike force of Nicola Zannini and Filippo Maniero.
